questions.question_text: Read the unseen passage segment context about a brave little sparrow building its nest. According to the text, why did the sparrow choose the thorny rosebush for its home?
options: A) It wanted to eat the rose petals.
B) The thorns provided natural protection from predators like cats and snakes.
C) It was the tallest plant in the garden.
D) The rosebush was closest to the birdbath.
questions.answer: B) The thorns provided natural protection from predators like cats and snakes.

questions.question_text: Based on the passage, what specific material did the sparrow struggle to find after the heavy rainstorm?
questions.answer: A) Dry twigs

questions.question_text: Which word from the passage means the same as 'persistent' or 'refusing to give up'?
questions.answer: B) Determined

questions.question_text: How did the garden owner help the little sparrow complete its nest after the storm damaged it? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: The garden owner noticed the bird's struggle and gently placed a handful of dry grass and small twigs on a low wall near the rosebush for the sparrow to easily collect.

questions.question_text: What does the sparrow's behavior teach us about facing difficulties in life? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: The sparrow's behavior teaches us resilience and hard work. Even when the heavy storm ruined its progress, the bird did not give up, but immediately started rebuilding its safe home.

questions.question_text: Give a suitable title for the passage based on the sparrow's actions, and justify your choice in one sentence. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: A suitable title is 'The Brave Little Builder'. This title is perfect because the passage entirely focuses on the sparrow's courage and constant effort to build a safe nest against all odds.

sections.section_name: Section B - Writing Skills & Applied Grammar

questions.question_text: Identify the subject and predicate in the following sentence: 'The old, wise owl hooted loudly in the dark forest.' [20-30 words]
questions.answer: The subject is 'The old, wise owl' because it is the doer of the action. The predicate is 'hooted loudly in the dark forest' because it describes what the subject did.

questions.question_text: Choose the correct abstract noun to complete the sentence: 'The king was known throughout the land for his immense __________.'
questions.answer: C) bravery

questions.question_text: Change the gender of the underlined noun and rewrite the sentence: 'The **emperor** rode his magnificent white horse into the courtyard.' [10-20 words]
questions.answer: The empress rode her magnificent white horse into the courtyard.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank with the correct personal pronoun: 'Riya and I are going to the library. Would you like to join _____?'
questions.answer: A) us

questions.question_text: Choose the correct degree of adjective: 'Mount Everest is the __________ mountain peak in the world.'
questions.answer: C) highest

questions.question_text: Insert the correct articles (a, an, the) in the blanks: 'I saw ___ eagle soaring high in ___ sky above the mountains.'
questions.answer: B) an, the

questions.question_text: Change the sentence to the Simple Past Tense: 'The dog catches the ball in mid-air.'
options: A) The dog is catching the ball in mid-air.
B) The dog has caught the ball in mid-air.
C) The dog caught the ball in mid-air.
D) The dog will catch the ball in mid-air.
questions.answer: C) The dog caught the ball in mid-air.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank with the correct modal verb of ability: 'When I was five years old, I __________ not swim at all.'
questions.answer: C) could

questions.question_text: Write a short diary entry expressing your feelings after winning the first prize in an inter-school debate competition. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Dear Diary, Today was a spectacular day! I finally won the first prize in the inter-school debate competition. I was so nervous before stepping onto the stage, but when I started speaking, all my fear vanished. Seeing the proud smiles on my parents' faces made all the hard work worth it. I feel incredibly happy and grateful tonight.

questions.question_text: Write a descriptive paragraph about your favorite festival, highlighting how you celebrate it with your family and its significance. [60-70 words]
questions.answer: My favorite festival is Diwali, the magnificent festival of lights. It signifies the victory of light over darkness and good over evil. Every year, my family and I clean our home thoroughly and decorate it with colorful rangolis, marigold flowers, and earthen diyas. In the evening, we perform a traditional pooja, share delicious homemade sweets with our neighbors, and enjoy watching the sky light up with eco-friendly sparklers. It is a time of immense joy and togetherness.

questions.question_text: Read the extract: 'He flattered the bird's beautiful voice, hoping she would sing and drop the cheese.' Which story is this from, and who is 'he'?
options: A) Rama to the Rescue; The monkey
B) The Raven and the Fox; The clever fox
C) What a Bird Thought; The farmer
D) The Unlikely Best Friends; The jackal
questions.answer: B) The Raven and the Fox; The clever fox

questions.question_text: Read the extract: 'Its leaves are bitter, but its benefits are sweet. It heals our skin and purifies the air.' What tree is the author referring to?
questions.answer: C) Neem Baba

questions.question_text: In the story 'A Bottle of Dew', why did Ramanatha spend years collecting dew drops instead of working on his land? [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Ramanatha was lazy and believed a fake sage's story that a magical potion could turn any metal into gold if mixed with five liters of winter dew. He wasted his years chasing this illusion instead of working.

questions.question_text: What is the central message conveyed in the poem 'A Friend's Prayer'? [30-40 words]
questions.answer: The poem conveys that a true friend does not judge or change us. Instead, a genuine friend accepts us with all our flaws, offering constant support, silent understanding, and a comforting presence during difficult times.

questions.question_text: In 'The Unlikely Best Friends', how did the animals prove that true friendship goes beyond differences in species? [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Despite being a deer, a crow, a mouse, and a tortoise, they used their unique abilities together as a team. They risked their own lives to rescue each other from the hunter's trap, proving their deep bond.

questions.question_text: In the poem 'What a Bird Thought', how did the bird's perception of the world change as it grew up? [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Initially, the bird thought the world was just a pale blue shell. Then it thought the world was made of leaves. Finally, when it flew into the open sky, it realized the world was vast and boundless.

questions.question_text: Discuss how Ramanatha's wife, Madhumati, cleverly taught him the value of hard work in 'A Bottle of Dew'. How did this change his life? [60-70 words]
questions.answer: Madhumati knew the magic potion was a lie, but she supported his dew collection on the condition that he plant bananas on their empty land to gather dew from the leaves. Over the years, while Ramanatha collected dew, she secretly sold the massive banana harvest in the market, saving a fortune. When the 'magic' failed, she showed him the box of gold coins earned from the crops, making him realize that hard work, not magic, brings true wealth.

questions.question_text: Analyze the moral of the fable 'The Raven and the Fox'. How does the fox's cunning manipulation serve as a warning to the readers against vanity and false praise? [60-70 words]
questions.answer: The fable teaches us to beware of flatterers who use fake praise for their own selfish gains. The fox wanted the piece of cheese held by the raven. Knowing the raven was vain, the fox falsely praised her beautiful singing voice. Blinded by pride, the raven opened her beak to sing, dropping the cheese directly to the fox. It serves as a strong warning that vanity and believing false compliments can lead to foolish mistakes and personal loss.
